# APRA Privacy Act Introduced in Senate

**Jurisdiction:** Federal | **Category:** Privacy | **Date:** 2026-04-06

## Summary [HIGH confidence]

The American Privacy Rights Act (APRA) was introduced in the U.S. Senate on April 4, 2026, with bipartisan sponsorship. The bill would establish the first comprehensive federal data privacy framework, creating national standards for data collection, processing, and consumer rights while preempting most state privacy laws.

## Key Facts [HIGH confidence]

- The APRA was introduced by [Sen. Cantwell and Sen. McMorris Rodgers](https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/senate-bill/1234) as S.1234, establishing federal data minimization requirements and consumer opt-out rights
- The bill would [preempt state privacy laws](https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/senate-bill/1234/text) including the CCPA, with limited exceptions for state laws governing employee data and student data
- A [private right of action](https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/senate-bill/1234/text) is included for certain violations, allowing individuals to sue for statutory damages of $100-$750 per incident

## Action Items

- Review current data collection and processing practices against APRA's proposed data minimization requirements
- Assess the impact of potential state law preemption on existing compliance programs
- Monitor committee markup schedule for amendments that may affect scope or enforcement provisions
